justification.mechanism: In high-income settings check dams and ponds trap sediment: loose-rock check dams on semi-arid USA rangeland watersheds retained 48.4% and 82.4% of total sediment yield and produced a twofold decline in outlet sediment per unit of peak runoff, four field-edge ponds in southern Germany trapped 54-85% of incoming sediment over 8 years, and a typical Belgian pond had a long-term trapping efficiency of 68% [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3]. Bench terracing in a small USA watershed reduced runoff by 9% and sediment yield by 58% [ev_runoff_reduction_meko14_1]. In Spain, terrace maintenance slowed runoff for events with a return period shorter than 8–10 years, and terraces in general interrupt flows, shrinking the runoff-contributing area and peak discharges (Bellin et al. 2009, cited in a review) [ev_runoff_reduction_arna15_5].
justification.conditionality: The studies found real effects in both directions, and what separates them is whether the structures hold and where erosion is measured. The gains are sediment trapped behind working dams, ponds and terraces; the harms are erosion triggered by the structures themselves or by their failure: channel incision was observed below 81% of surveyed check dams in a Spanish catchment through the clear-water effect [ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1], about 30 years after channel runoff-control structures on semi-arid Arizona rangelands were abandoned a large share had failed and some accelerated headcut retreat and scouring (Nichols et al. 2018) [ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_12], and in the Israeli Negev traditional stone terraces across dry channels proved highly vulnerable to collapse, their failure inducing rill and gully erosion, so they need frequent maintenance [ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_13]. For a Task Team Leader the separators are maintenance over decades and design for the channel below the structure. Even working check dams had no statistically significant effect on the runoff volume of major storms, reducing only the number of runoff events from small storms by 60%, and the twofold decline in outlet sediment was significant only at α = 0.2 [ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_2, ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_1, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]. Most units are secondary citations in reviews, and the high-income settings (rangeland, arable fields with ponds, Mediterranean terraces) differ from smallholder water harvesting [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_runoff_reduction_arna15_5].

effect_mechanism: Physical SWC works under public-works and watershed programmes reduce soil loss and downstream runoff, and sediment-control dams with terraces and vegetation trap sediment in the catchment. A meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds soil loss cut by 58.66% and runoff by 53% on average, with soil and stone bunds reducing soil loss by 55.06% and runoff by 49.2% [ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_1, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_1, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_4, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_5]; in Ethiopian catchments, stone bunds, check dams and vegetation regrowth cut sediment yield from 8.5 to 1.9 t per hectare a year [ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_1, ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_2]. Ethiopian catchment studies cited in a review report physical soil and water conservation decreasing runoff by up to 88% (Taye et al., 2015; Haregeweyn et al., 2015), and integrated catchment management at May Zeg Zeg cutting surface runoff volume by 81% (Nyssen et al., 2010) [ev_runoff_reduction_gebr18_7, ev_runoff_reduction_gebr18_8].
conditionality: Nearly all units are programme or lender reports from Ethiopia, India and China, often perception surveys or before/after comparisons; an Uttarakhand water budget showed surface runoff slightly increasing, the Karnataka runoff comparison is against another SWC programme, and IEG doubts the India runoff measurements. Effects mixing runoff and soil-loss metrics are only components of erosion risk. A catchment-restoration meta-analysis in Ethiopia finds minimal effect of catchment treatment on runoff in drought-prone areas with annual rainfall below 500 mm [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_3]. The Ethiopian catchment results combine structures with grazing control and vegetation regeneration and are cited in a review, so the share due to the works is not isolated [ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_1]. The 88% and 81% runoff figures are cited second-hand: the first is an upper bound, and the second is a before-and-after result for a catchment-management package rather than the structures alone [ev_runoff_reduction_gebr18_7, ev_runoff_reduction_gebr18_8].

justification.conditionality: Confidence is only medium because the row rests on practitioner ratings from the Burkina Faso and Kenyan WOCAT technology sheets; no literature measurement of soil loss covers this family, and the rated reduction says nothing about how much sediment leaves the treated area [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_2895_2017_soil_loss].

effect_mechanism: Check dams, gabions, fascines and gully plugs trap sediment in gullies and channels, reducing catchment sediment export, and hill reservoirs reduce outlet flows [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_4]. WOCAT compilers describe masonry check dams in Ethiopia slowing runoff so soil accumulates upstream, gabions and rock check dams in Somalia cutting runoff speed and gully expansion, controlled runoff reducing erosion close to a Somali haffir, and a Cambodian pond allowing crops in all seasons as vegetation cover [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7778_2026_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7777_2026_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_soil_loss]. Check dams on China's Loess Plateau reduced erosion rates from more than 200 to 20–25 t per hectare a year and cut regional runoff and sediment by about 15% and 85%, check dams at the outlets of five Chinese catchments accounted for 37.2% to 72.2% of sediment reduction over 26 years, vegetated check dams in northern Ethiopia significantly reduced peak flow and runoff volume, loose-rock check dams on USA rangeland retained 48.4% and 82.4% of sediment yield, and small ponds in Germany and Belgium trapped 54-85% and 68% of incoming sediment [ev_erosion_hazard_luca21_1, ev_runoff_reduction_luca21_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_4, ev_runoff_reduction_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3]. In Brazil, barraginhas dispersed across farms capture runoff water, which Embrapa says prevents erosion, siltation and the carrying of pollutants [ev_runoff_reduction_mira19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_mira19_5]. Well-designed concrete or masonry check dams reduce stream power, sediment transport and channel erosion (Liu 1992, cited in a review) [ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_11]. On China's Loess Plateau, a watershed model found check-dam construction cut runoff by 12% and sediment by 11.7%, check dams in the Yanhe watershed cut rainy-season runoff by 15.5%–28.9% (Xu et al. 2013), and check dams cut the sediment load of the Huangfuchuan catchment by 51.9% in a sediment delivery model (Zhao et al. 2017) [ev_runoff_reduction_shi19_1, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_2, ev_runoff_reduction_shi19_6, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_8].
conditionality: The WOCAT units are practitioner ratings; the pooled sediment figures come from a single check-dam synthesis, so the independent literature base is narrow [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_fran21_3]. Check dams can cause downstream channel incision through the clear-water effect (documented in Spain, a high-income setting), gabions in Morocco have filled and need raising to keep working, and the Ethiopian compiler notes that the visible siltation held back has not been quantified [ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_1, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6716_2023_downstream_siltation]. USA check dams had no significant effect on the runoff volume of major storms and their reduction of outlet sediment was significant only at α = 0.2 [ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_2, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]; the Chinese, Ethiopian and European figures are secondary citations in reviews, and the USA and European sites are high-income [ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_1]. The barraginha erosion statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measurement [ev_runoff_reduction_mira19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_mira19_5]. Structures that are abandoned or collapse can turn into erosion sources: decades after channel runoff-control structures on Arizona rangelands were abandoned, a large share had failed and some accelerated headcut retreat and scouring, and failed stone terraces across dry channels in the Israeli Negev induced rill and gully erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_12, ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_13]. The Loess Plateau figures are model results, partly cited second-hand [ev_runoff_reduction_shi19_1, ev_runoff_reduction_shi19_6, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_8].

effect_mechanism: Spate and water-spreading structures control flood flows on the land: in Yemen spate development reduces damage to wadi banks and lets areas re-green, with 64% of the farmers interviewed emphasising the reduced erosion, and the Ethiopian compiler for water-spreading weirs says the physical barriers stop soil and water loss [ev_erosion_hazard_yem12_5, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_soil_loss].
conditionality: The Yemen figure is a share of farmers who perceived the benefit, reported in a lender completion report, not a measured soil loss, and the Ethiopian unit is a practitioner rating from a WOCAT sheet [ev_erosion_hazard_yem12_5, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_soil_loss]. Neither gives the size of the reduction in soil loss, so the class rests on direction and rating rather than on a measured effect.

effect_mechanism: Bench and progressive terraces, contour stone bunds and lines and banquettes shorten slope length and slow runoff, so soil losses on steep plots fall sharply and sediment loads drop where terracing is widespread. Terraces cut soil losses on small mountain plots on 20 to 60% slopes from more than 200 to under 2 t/ha a year, a contour banquette in Niger divided erosion by 150 against traditional cropping, and stone bunds with compost cut total soil loss by 79% [ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_zoug14_1]. WOCAT compilers for bench terraces in Thailand, contour stone bunds in Bhutan and Gradoni terraces in Uzbekistan rate soil loss or runoff as reduced, the Uzbek compiler noting that soil eroded from the inter-spaces is trapped by the terraces [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_4281_2018_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6891_2023_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7553_2025_surface_runoff]. Meta-analyses agree: a terracing meta-analysis finds erosion control on terraces 11.46 times that of controls and runoff reduction 2.6 times [ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1, ev_runoff_reduction_wei16_1], a meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds terraces cut soil loss by 60.21% and runoff by 56.5%, and an Ethiopian synthesis reports stone bunds cutting soil loss by 38% and runoff by 34.4% [ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_5, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_3, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_3, ev_runoff_reduction_adim16_3]. Reviews also report terracing reducing runoff by 92.6% and 80% in sub-humid and humid regions, stone lines and terraces reducing runoff and erosion by 30 to 50%, sediment accumulating behind Ethiopian stone bunds at 59 t per hectare a year, and fanya juu trapping 64% of sediment, rising to 80% with vetiver grass [ev_runoff_reduction_wei16_2, ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_3, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_6]. Reviews add further cited contrasts: runoff and erosion in non-terraced catchments 2.7 and 15.3 times higher than in terraced ones under the same cultivation (Lal, 1982), stone-terraced hillslopes reducing runoff by 65–85% and soil erosion by 58–69% (Al-Seekh and Mohammad, 2009), stone bunds reducing soil erosion by 68% (Nyssen et al., 2007), soil loss in Dogu'a Tembien falling from 57 to 20 t per hectare a year after physical conservation (Gebremichael et al., 2005), and modelled net erosion of 25.04 t per hectare a year on terrace farmland against 28.97 on slope farmland in China's Dingjiagou catchment (Zhang and Li, 2014) [ev_runoff_reduction_arna15_1, ev_runoff_reduction_stav20_1, ev_erosion_hazard_gebr18_1, ev_erosion_hazard_gebr18_13, ev_erosion_hazard_arna15_3]. A review of farming terraces explains why: terraces increase infiltration rates, reduce sediment transport and interrupt the flows that feed runoff contribution areas and peak discharges [ev_erosion_hazard_arna15_4, ev_runoff_reduction_arna15_5].
conditionality: Alignment decides the sign: diversion banquettes in Niger doubled runoff coefficients and increased gully erosion, while contour banquettes in the same region cut erosion; ditches with downslope banks cause rill erosion, many Maghreb banquettes were erased or unmaintained, and abandoned terraces increase erosion [ev_runoff_reduction_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_4, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_2]. The Rwanda sediment reductions are lender-monitored before/after figures without a control, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements rather than measurements [ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_2]. Bench terracing alone reduced runoff by only 9% in a small USA watershed, gullied area on Tunisian banquette land grew by 12% between 1963 and 1973, poorly maintained Algerian banquettes accelerate erosion, and Algerian banquettes had no influence on downstream dam sedimentation [ev_runoff_reduction_meko14_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]. The meta-analytic ratios are unweighted, and the Ethiopian stone-bund sediment figure comes with a total soil loss of 77 t per hectare, so bunds trap most but not all eroded soil [ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1]. Construction can also cause harm: in cropland fields, excessive removal of stones to build terraces has been linked to a threefold increase in sheet and rill erosion (Nyssen et al., 2007, cited by Stavi et al.) [ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_3]. Terraces do not hold everything: the review puts the delivery ratio at approximately 20%–30% for sediment and 50%–60% for runoff, and in extreme rainfall the sediment accumulated on terraces can reach the channel; in a Spanish catchment, terrace maintenance slowed runoff only for events with a return period shorter than 8–10 years (Bellin et al., 2009) [ev_sediment_retention_arna15_6, ev_runoff_reduction_arna15_5]. The Dingjiagou difference is modelled and small, and the review contrasts are cited second-hand [ev_erosion_hazard_arna15_3].

justification.mechanism: Bench and progressive terraces, contour stone bunds and lines and banquettes shorten slope length and slow runoff, so soil losses on steep plots fall sharply and sediment loads drop where terracing is widespread. Terraces cut soil losses on small mountain plots on 20 to 60% slopes from more than 200 to under 2 t/ha a year, a contour banquette in Niger divided erosion by 150 against traditional cropping, and stone bunds with compost cut total soil loss by 79% [ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_zoug14_1]. WOCAT compilers for bench terraces in Thailand, contour stone bunds in Bhutan and Gradoni terraces in Uzbekistan rate soil loss or runoff as reduced, the Uzbek compiler noting that soil eroded from the inter-spaces is trapped by the terraces [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_4281_2018_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6891_2023_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7553_2025_surface_runoff]. Meta-analyses agree: a terracing meta-analysis finds erosion control on terraces 11.46 times that of controls and runoff reduction 2.6 times [ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1, ev_runoff_reduction_wei16_1], a meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds terraces cut soil loss by 60.21% and runoff by 56.5%, and an Ethiopian synthesis reports stone bunds cutting soil loss by 38% and runoff by 34.4% [ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_5, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_3, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_3, ev_runoff_reduction_adim16_3]. Reviews also report terracing reducing runoff by 92.6% and 80% in sub-humid and humid regions, stone lines and terraces reducing runoff and erosion by 30 to 50%, sediment accumulating behind Ethiopian stone bunds at 59 t per hectare a year, and fanya juu trapping 64% of sediment, rising to 80% with vetiver grass [ev_runoff_reduction_wei16_2, ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_3, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_6]. Reviews add further cited contrasts: runoff and erosion in non-terraced catchments 2.7 and 15.3 times higher than in terraced ones under the same cultivation (Lal, 1982), stone-terraced hillslopes reducing runoff by 65–85% and soil erosion by 58–69% (Al-Seekh and Mohammad, 2009), stone bunds reducing soil erosion by 68% (Nyssen et al., 2007), soil loss in Dogu'a Tembien falling from 57 to 20 t per hectare a year after physical conservation (Gebremichael et al., 2005), and modelled net erosion of 25.04 t per hectare a year on terrace farmland against 28.97 on slope farmland in China's Dingjiagou catchment (Zhang and Li, 2014) [ev_runoff_reduction_arna15_1, ev_runoff_reduction_stav20_1, ev_erosion_hazard_gebr18_1, ev_erosion_hazard_gebr18_13, ev_erosion_hazard_arna15_3]. A review of farming terraces explains why: terraces increase infiltration rates, reduce sediment transport and interrupt the flows that feed runoff contribution areas and peak discharges [ev_erosion_hazard_arna15_4, ev_runoff_reduction_arna15_5].
justification.conditionality: Alignment decides the sign: diversion banquettes in Niger doubled runoff coefficients and increased gully erosion, while contour banquettes in the same region cut erosion; ditches with downslope banks cause rill erosion, many Maghreb banquettes were erased or unmaintained, and abandoned terraces increase erosion [ev_runoff_reduction_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_4, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_2]. The Rwanda sediment reductions are lender-monitored before/after figures without a control, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements rather than measurements [ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_2]. Bench terracing alone reduced runoff by only 9% in a small USA watershed, gullied area on Tunisian banquette land grew by 12% between 1963 and 1973, poorly maintained Algerian banquettes accelerate erosion, and Algerian banquettes had no influence on downstream dam sedimentation [ev_runoff_reduction_meko14_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]. The meta-analytic ratios are unweighted, and the Ethiopian stone-bund sediment figure comes with a total soil loss of 77 t per hectare, so bunds trap most but not all eroded soil [ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1]. Construction can also cause harm: in cropland fields, excessive removal of stones to build terraces has been linked to a threefold increase in sheet and rill erosion (Nyssen et al., 2007, cited by Stavi et al.) [ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_3]. Terraces do not hold everything: the review puts the delivery ratio at approximately 20%–30% for sediment and 50%–60% for runoff, and in extreme rainfall the sediment accumulated on terraces can reach the channel; in a Spanish catchment, terrace maintenance slowed runoff only for events with a return period shorter than 8–10 years (Bellin et al., 2009) [ev_sediment_retention_arna15_6, ev_runoff_reduction_arna15_5]. The Dingjiagou difference is modelled and small, and the review contrasts are cited second-hand [ev_erosion_hazard_arna15_3].

effect_mechanism: Check dams, gabions, fascines, terraces and bunds trap sediment that would otherwise reach streams, canals and reservoirs, lowering catchment sediment export and downstream siltation [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_3]. WOCAT compilers describe gabion walls and check dams in Somalia trapping sediment upstream so less travels downstream, and a masonry check dam in Ethiopia holding back visible siltation [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_7778_2026_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6716_2023_downstream_siltation]. Measured retention now spans scales: check dams on China's Loess Plateau are credited with cutting regional sediment export by about 85% and accounted for 37.2% to 72.2% of sediment reduction at the outlets of five catchments over 26 years, studies cited by Shi et al. report check dams cutting sediment by 79.4%–85.5% in the Yanhe watershed and the sediment load by 51.9% in the Huangfuchuan catchment, and a watershed model attributes an 11.7% sediment reduction to the main check dams [ev_sediment_retention_shi19_7, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_8, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_2]; loose-rock check dams on semi-arid USA rangeland retained 48.4% and 82.4% of watershed sediment yield [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_4, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1]; sediment accumulates behind Ethiopian stone bunds at 59 t per hectare a year, fanya juu trapped 64% of sediment (80% with vetiver grass), and bench terracing cut sediment yield by 58% in a small USA watershed [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_6, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_5]; and small ponds trapped 54-85% of incoming sediment over 8 years in southern Germany and 68% over the long term in Belgium [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3]. Holding soil also holds nutrients: an Ethiopian synthesis finds graded soil bunds reduced total nitrogen lost in runoff and sediment by up to 48% [ev_nutrient_removal_adim16_1].
conditionality: The class follows the sub-practice vote, not the pooled result. The in-field row holds the strongest result, strong, but it rests on the Ethiopian graded-bund nitrogen synthesis [ev_nutrient_removal_adim16_1]. The rows that carry the measured trapping studies — check dams and ponds (runoff catchment) and terraces and bunds (terracing) — hold moderate, and the cross-family row, a single modelled Chinese programme figure, holds slight [ev_sediment_retention_iegchn07_5]. The vote gives moderate, below the pooled strong. Water quality is inferred almost entirely from sediment retention, a component proxy, plus nutrient losses in runoff from a single synthesis; nothing on water chemistry downstream is measured, and the WOCAT units are practitioner ratings of downstream siltation. Retention is partial: a terracing review puts the delivery ratio at about 20%–30% for sediment, and in extreme rainfall the sediment held on terraces can reach the channel [ev_sediment_retention_arna15_6]. Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of a downstream dam over 1947-1968, and the twofold decline in outlet sediment yield with USA check dams was significant only at α = 0.2 [ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]. Much of the literature is secondary citations in reviews, several from high-income settings (USA, Germany, Belgium), the China programme figure and the Loess Plateau watershed results are modelled [ev_sediment_retention_shi19_2, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_7], and gabions in Morocco have filled and need raising [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_sediment_retention_iegchn07_5, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_1]. The Ethiopian compiler notes the trapped sediment has not been quantified [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6716_2023_downstream_siltation].

effect_mechanism: Check dams trap sediment before it reaches rivers and reservoirs: on China's Loess Plateau a check-dam campaign to retain floodwater and intercept soil sediments is credited with reducing sediment by about 85%, and at the outlets of five Chinese catchments check dams accounted for sediment reductions of 37.2% to 72.2% over 26 years compared with other soil and water conservation measures [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_4]. Further Loess Plateau studies agree: check dams in the Yanhe watershed cut sediment by 79.4%–85.5% (Xu et al. 2013), a sediment delivery model credits check dams with removing 51.9% of the Huangfuchuan sediment load (Zhao et al. 2017), and a watershed model found the main check dams cut sediment by 11.7% [ev_sediment_retention_shi19_7, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_8, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_2].
conditionality: Not every work cuts downstream sediment: Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of the Oued Fodda dam over 1947-1968 [ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]. effect_mechanism: Check dams, gabions and ponds store sediment in channels, reducing catchment sediment yield and the topsoil washed downstream [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_1]. WOCAT compilers rate downstream siltation as reduced for gabions and check dams in Somalia that trap sediment upstream, and for a masonry check dam in Ethiopia that holds back visible siltation [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_7778_2026_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6716_2023_downstream_siltation]. In the literature check dams on China's Loess Plateau are credited with cutting regional sediment export by about 85% and accounted for 37.2% to 72.2% of sediment reduction at the outlets of five catchments over 26 years, and loose-rock check dams on semi-arid USA rangeland retained 48.4% and 82.4% of watershed sediment yield [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_4, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1], and small ponds trapped 54-85% of incoming sediment over 8 years in southern Germany and 68% over the long term in Belgium [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3]. Modelling on the Loess Plateau gives a similar picture: a SWAT simulation found check dam construction decreased sediment by 11.7%, and studies cited in the same paper attribute a 79.4%–85.5% sediment decrease in the Yanhe watershed (Xu et al., 2013) and a 51.9% cut in sediment load in the Huangfuchuan catchment (Zhao et al., 2017) to check dams [ev_sediment_retention_shi19_2, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_7, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_8].
conditionality: Sediment retention is a component proxy for water quality, and nothing on downstream water chemistry is measured; the pooled check-dam magnitudes come from a single synthesis, the Ethiopian compiler notes the trapped sediment has not been quantified, and gabions in Morocco have filled up and need raising to keep trapping sediment [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_1]. The other figures are mostly secondary citations in reviews, the USA, German and Belgian sites are high-income, and the twofold decline in outlet sediment at the USA sites was significant only at α = 0.2 [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]. The Loess Plateau figures are all model estimates, and the range between them (from 11.7% to over 79.4%) shows how much the result depends on the catchment and on how many dams are modelled [ev_sediment_retention_shi19_2, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_7].

effect_mechanism: Bunds, stone lines, micro-basins and check dams capture and retain rainwater so that it infiltrates, and compilers and local people report raised well levels; sand dams and subsurface dams store water that extends the months of water access or backs up wells when other sources dry up, production cisterns keep livestock watered, and participating villages in India reduced water transport by tanker. WOCAT compilers for the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso, a sand dam in Kenya, a farm pond in Cambodia, stone lines in Tunisia and haffir and gabion works in Somalia judge them to improve water harvesting, water quantity or water availability [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1528_2012_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1537_2012_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_2844_2017_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6610_2022_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7777_2026_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7778_2026_water_quantity]. In Zimbabwe the months per year water could be collected at sand-dam sites rose from 6.5 to 10.9 after construction, and from 5.8 to 9.7 in a drought year, while in Kenya the average distance to a water source fell from 3 to 1 km [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lasage08_1]. A check-dam review reports that check dams storing seasonal runoff solve local supply scarcity; traditional rainwater ponds in South Korea reduced the occurrence of water deficit from 30 to 20% [ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1]. In India, discharge of springs and streams rose in treated watersheds: a sample study in Himachal Pradesh reports a 40 percent increase in water discharge in spring and stream sources [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1], and the Uttarakhand project achieved an average 21 percent increase in water discharge from perennial water sources in sampled micro-watersheds, against a target of 25 percent [ev_water_regulation_utk22_6]. Measured soil moisture adds a field-level route: capture structures hold rain in the root zone. A meta-analysis of in-situ practices finds they improve soil moisture retention by 59%, with infiltration pits highest at an SMD of 114.4%, soil/stone bunds 76.4%, tied ridging 48.9% and terraces 40.5% [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_1, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_2, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_3, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_5, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_6]; a global terracing synthesis finds terraced sites more efficient than slopes at conserving soil water, with a mean δsm of 1.2 [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1]; and conversion of slopeland to leveled fields in China increased moisture retention [ev_soil_water_retention_iegchn07_2]. In Burkina Faso, zaï of 30–40 cm diameter and 1-m half-moons retained moisture for 2-3 weeks through dry spells, and zaï can retain moisture in the soil for seven to ten days after rainfall [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8]. In Brazil tied furrows kept more soil moisture than the traditional flat system at all crop stages and depths [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9], and in Ethiopia hand-dug planting basins held more topsoil water than unmulched plots at Ziway at flowering and maturity [ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_4, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_6]. Mulching, the soil-cover form of in-situ water harvesting, improves soil moisture retention with an SMD of 54.0% in the meta-analysis, and maize-stalk mulch in Ethiopia held more topsoil water than unmulched plots at Ziway at all three stages [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_4, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_1, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_3, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_5]. Indian project watersheds showed an increase in soil moisture content by 30.5 percent compared to the IWMP sites [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2]. Water productivity, the grain produced per unit of rain, is a route by which capture eases water stress. Grain per unit of rain rises with capture in a set of East and Southern African trials: the best conservation-farming practice per site gave yield increases ranging from 20 to 120% over conventional tillage whilst rain water productivity improved with 10–50% [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_1]. In an on-farm trial at Houndé, Burkina Faso, stone rows with zaï pits, every arm also receiving manure, lifted maize rain water productivity from 3.10 kg per hectare per mm under the farmers' practice of oxen ploughing with NPK and urea to 6.61 [ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_1]. A review reports that contour tied-ridging in eastern Sudan gave the highest water use efficiency of the treatments compared [ev_rain_water_productivity_ngur26_3]. The water-productivity evidence points the same way: FAO compilers list improved water use efficiency among the main benefits of rainwater harvesting, the WOCAT guideline authors find that all water harvesting groups indicate improved water use efficiency, mostly high to medium, through reduced evaporation loss and better soil water availability, and a review sentence, citing earlier work, says capture approaches often lead also to higher water productivity because denser canopies shade the soil [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1]. FAO compilers rate improving water productivity for the cross-slope barrier group at the middle mark of their scale [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3]. Trials and reviews add to the soil-moisture route: micro-catchments in Ethiopia raised mean soil moisture by 31% in the wet season and 24% in the dry season (cited in a review), tied ridging, open ridging and sub-soiling raised root-zone water by 24%, 15% and 3% over traditional tillage in drought-stricken Wollo (McHugh et al. 2007), tied ridges in northern Ethiopia cut runoff by about 60% and raised rooting-zone water by at least 13% (Araya and Stroosnijder 2010), terraces stay humid longer than sloping fields (Posthumus and Stroosnijder 2010), and 20–25 cm deep contour furrows in Iran raised soil moisture and shrub productivity (Jahantigh and Pessarakli 2009) [ev_soil_moisture_biaz12_1, ev_soil_moisture_biaz12_6, ev_soil_moisture_dile13_1, ev_soil_moisture_biaz12_8, ev_soil_moisture_arna15_7, ev_soil_moisture_stav20_6]. On water productivity, terraces in Ethiopia improved the water productivity of three crops by at least 100% against un-terraced plots [ev_rain_water_productivity_adgo13_7], tied ridging with a wood-shavings mulch raised rainfall water-use efficiency of sorghum in Nigeria [ev_rain_water_productivity_chir06_9], and supplemental irrigation from a Kenyan runoff dam with fertiliser raised rain and irrigation water-use efficiency from 2.1 to 4.1 kg of grain per mm per hectare [ev_rain_water_productivity_barr05_9]; supplementary irrigation in semi-arid Zimbabwe raised water productivity from 1.75 to 2.3 kg per cubic metre (Kahinda et al. 2007) [ev_rain_water_productivity_dile13_6, ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5]. In Burkina Faso, water-harvesting reservoirs are used for livestock and household needs during periods of domestic water scarcity [ev_water_access_deficit_foxr03_7].
conditionality: The class follows the sub-practice vote, not the pooled result: the storage and cross-family rows hold strong results and the in-field, micro-catchment and terracing rows moderate ones, so the roll-up is moderate rather than the pooled strong. Most literature units are narrative, perception or lender-reported, the pooled percentages mix spring-discharge, water-deficit and tanker-use metrics, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets rather than measurements [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1528_2012_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7778_2026_water_availability]. Groundwater-recharge evidence, with its limits, now sits in the catchment water yield rows. Many sand dams cannot supply a household through the dry season [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3]. The Zimbabwean sand-dam figures rely on recall of conditions before construction [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2]. The check-dam and pond findings are secondary citations in reviews, and the Korean result is modelled in a high-income setting [ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1]. The Indian spring and stream discharge figures come from World Bank completion reports, the lender's own evaluation, measured before and after without untreated comparison sites, for catchment treatment that bundles plantations, trenches, ponds and check dams with water-harvesting structures, so the gain cannot be credited to water harvesting alone [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1, ev_water_regulation_utk22_6]. What upstream capture does to water downstream is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows. The measured soil-moisture evidence has its own limits. Tillage alone is not water harvesting: in the Brazilian trial deep ploughing, which is tillage alone, scored as high as the tied furrows, so that treatment does not speak for the practice [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9]. The Ethiopian basins did not differ from unmulched plots at planting at Ziway or at any stage at Melkassa [ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_2, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_8, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_10, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_12]. Under meteorological drought and dry spells in Kenya, tied ridging without organic inputs was insufficient in soil moisture conservation since there was little or no rainwater to be held in the basins [ev_soil_water_retention_ndun23_1]: structures store rain, they cannot make it. A review found no significant effect of infiltration trenches on soil moisture because only four studies provided sufficient statistical data [ev_soil_water_retention_locat20_1]. The zaï and half-moon results come with compost in the pits, so the moisture gain cannot be credited to the pit alone [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8], the Indian watershed comparison is a project-commissioned study of a package of soil and water conservation structures [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2], and the Brazilian tied-furrow trial ran a single season at a station of the agency that promotes the technology [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9]. Soil moisture is read as a component of water stress, not water stress itself. Those best-practice arms are bundled: planting pits, basins or ripper-with-ridging (the capture element, which is the practice here) come with reduced tillage and mostly with fertiliser, and tillage alone is not water harvesting [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_1]. The trial-level readings are weaker: the authors find no clear tillage effect on rain water productivity in Kenya, no clear effects of tillage in Ethiopia (where the gains that do show come with fertilised treatments), and only a tendency of improvement in semi-arid Tanzania [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_5, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_4]. The Burkina Faso trial covers a single season, and every conservation arm also received manure, so its gain belongs to the package rather than to the structures alone [ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_1]. At Houndé, grass strips with zaï (4.84 against 3.10) were not significantly different from the control, and at Péni neither grass strips with zaï (4.51) nor earth bunds with contour ploughing (4.31) differed significantly from the control (3.53), the authors stating that water was not limiting at Péni, which had more rain than Houndé that season [ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_2, ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_4]. The Sudan comparison ranks treatments without a no-practice value [ev_rain_water_productivity_ngur26_3]. These are compiler and author judgements across groups, direction only, and the review sentence is second-hand; the WOCAT authors also note that some case studies indicate little to no improvement in water use efficiency [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1]. The FAO cross-slope barrier mark is a compiler judgement, direction only [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3]. The water-productivity and moisture gains are not universal: ridging without a mulch did not consistently raise water-use efficiency in Nigeria, overall rain-plus-irrigation water-use efficiency did not rise with supplemental irrigation in Burkina Faso, and Nigerian ridges stored a few per cent more soil water each year but significantly so on only a single measurement date out of nine [ev_rain_water_productivity_chir06_8, ev_rain_water_productivity_foxr03_6, ev_soil_moisture_chir06_7]. The Nigerian water-use gain is bundled with mulch, and most of the Ethiopian, Iranian and terrace moisture figures are cited second-hand [ev_rain_water_productivity_chir06_9, ev_soil_moisture_biaz12_1].

justification.mechanism: Bunds, stone lines, micro-basins and check dams capture and retain rainwater so that it infiltrates, and compilers and local people report raised well levels; sand dams and subsurface dams store water that extends the months of water access or backs up wells when other sources dry up, production cisterns keep livestock watered, and participating villages in India reduced water transport by tanker. WOCAT compilers for the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso, a sand dam in Kenya, a farm pond in Cambodia, stone lines in Tunisia and haffir and gabion works in Somalia judge them to improve water harvesting, water quantity or water availability [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1528_2012_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1537_2012_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_2844_2017_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6610_2022_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7777_2026_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7778_2026_water_quantity]. In Zimbabwe the months per year water could be collected at sand-dam sites rose from 6.5 to 10.9 after construction, and from 5.8 to 9.7 in a drought year, while in Kenya the average distance to a water source fell from 3 to 1 km [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lasage08_1]. A check-dam review reports that check dams storing seasonal runoff solve local supply scarcity; traditional rainwater ponds in South Korea reduced the occurrence of water deficit from 30 to 20% [ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1]. In India, discharge of springs and streams rose in treated watersheds: a sample study in Himachal Pradesh reports a 40 percent increase in water discharge in spring and stream sources [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1], and the Uttarakhand project achieved an average 21 percent increase in water discharge from perennial water sources in sampled micro-watersheds, against a target of 25 percent [ev_water_regulation_utk22_6]. Measured soil moisture adds a field-level route: capture structures hold rain in the root zone. A meta-analysis of in-situ practices finds they improve soil moisture retention by 59%, with infiltration pits highest at an SMD of 114.4%, soil/stone bunds 76.4%, tied ridging 48.9% and terraces 40.5% [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_1, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_2, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_3, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_5, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_6]; a global terracing synthesis finds terraced sites more efficient than slopes at conserving soil water, with a mean δsm of 1.2 [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1]; and conversion of slopeland to leveled fields in China increased moisture retention [ev_soil_water_retention_iegchn07_2]. In Burkina Faso, zaï of 30–40 cm diameter and 1-m half-moons retained moisture for 2-3 weeks through dry spells, and zaï can retain moisture in the soil for seven to ten days after rainfall [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8]. In Brazil tied furrows kept more soil moisture than the traditional flat system at all crop stages and depths [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9], and in Ethiopia hand-dug planting basins held more topsoil water than unmulched plots at Ziway at flowering and maturity [ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_4, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_6]. Mulching, the soil-cover form of in-situ water harvesting, improves soil moisture retention with an SMD of 54.0% in the meta-analysis, and maize-stalk mulch in Ethiopia held more topsoil water than unmulched plots at Ziway at all three stages [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_4, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_1, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_3, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_5]. Indian project watersheds showed an increase in soil moisture content by 30.5 percent compared to the IWMP sites [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2]. Water productivity, the grain produced per unit of rain, is a route by which capture eases water stress. Grain per unit of rain rises with capture in a set of East and Southern African trials: the best conservation-farming practice per site gave yield increases ranging from 20 to 120% over conventional tillage whilst rain water productivity improved with 10–50% [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_1]. In an on-farm trial at Houndé, Burkina Faso, stone rows with zaï pits, every arm also receiving manure, lifted maize rain water productivity from 3.10 kg per hectare per mm under the farmers' practice of oxen ploughing with NPK and urea to 6.61 [ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_1]. A review reports that contour tied-ridging in eastern Sudan gave the highest water use efficiency of the treatments compared [ev_rain_water_productivity_ngur26_3]. The water-productivity evidence points the same way: FAO compilers list improved water use efficiency among the main benefits of rainwater harvesting, the WOCAT guideline authors find that all water harvesting groups indicate improved water use efficiency, mostly high to medium, through reduced evaporation loss and better soil water availability, and a review sentence, citing earlier work, says capture approaches often lead also to higher water productivity because denser canopies shade the soil [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1]. FAO compilers rate improving water productivity for the cross-slope barrier group at the middle mark of their scale [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3]. Trials and reviews add to the soil-moisture route: micro-catchments in Ethiopia raised mean soil moisture by 31% in the wet season and 24% in the dry season (cited in a review), tied ridging, open ridging and sub-soiling raised root-zone water by 24%, 15% and 3% over traditional tillage in drought-stricken Wollo (McHugh et al. 2007), tied ridges in northern Ethiopia cut runoff by about 60% and raised rooting-zone water by at least 13% (Araya and Stroosnijder 2010), terraces stay humid longer than sloping fields (Posthumus and Stroosnijder 2010), and 20–25 cm deep contour furrows in Iran raised soil moisture and shrub productivity (Jahantigh and Pessarakli 2009) [ev_soil_moisture_biaz12_1, ev_soil_moisture_biaz12_6, ev_soil_moisture_dile13_1, ev_soil_moisture_biaz12_8, ev_soil_moisture_arna15_7, ev_soil_moisture_stav20_6]. On water productivity, terraces in Ethiopia improved the water productivity of three crops by at least 100% against un-terraced plots [ev_rain_water_productivity_adgo13_7], tied ridging with a wood-shavings mulch raised rainfall water-use efficiency of sorghum in Nigeria [ev_rain_water_productivity_chir06_9], and supplemental irrigation from a Kenyan runoff dam with fertiliser raised rain and irrigation water-use efficiency from 2.1 to 4.1 kg of grain per mm per hectare [ev_rain_water_productivity_barr05_9]; supplementary irrigation in semi-arid Zimbabwe raised water productivity from 1.75 to 2.3 kg per cubic metre (Kahinda et al. 2007) [ev_rain_water_productivity_dile13_6, ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5]. In Burkina Faso, water-harvesting reservoirs are used for livestock and household needs during periods of domestic water scarcity [ev_water_access_deficit_foxr03_7].
justification.conditionality: The class follows the sub-practice vote, not the pooled result: the storage and cross-family rows hold strong results and the in-field, micro-catchment and terracing rows moderate ones, so the roll-up is moderate rather than the pooled strong. Most literature units are narrative, perception or lender-reported, the pooled percentages mix spring-discharge, water-deficit and tanker-use metrics, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets rather than measurements [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1528_2012_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7778_2026_water_availability]. Groundwater-recharge evidence, with its limits, now sits in the catchment water yield rows. Many sand dams cannot supply a household through the dry season [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3]. The Zimbabwean sand-dam figures rely on recall of conditions before construction [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2]. The check-dam and pond findings are secondary citations in reviews, and the Korean result is modelled in a high-income setting [ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1]. The Indian spring and stream discharge figures come from World Bank completion reports, the lender's own evaluation, measured before and after without untreated comparison sites, for catchment treatment that bundles plantations, trenches, ponds and check dams with water-harvesting structures, so the gain cannot be credited to water harvesting alone [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1, ev_water_regulation_utk22_6]. What upstream capture does to water downstream is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows. The measured soil-moisture evidence has its own limits. Tillage alone is not water harvesting: in the Brazilian trial deep ploughing, which is tillage alone, scored as high as the tied furrows, so that treatment does not speak for the practice [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9]. The Ethiopian basins did not differ from unmulched plots at planting at Ziway or at any stage at Melkassa [ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_2, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_8, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_10, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_12]. Under meteorological drought and dry spells in Kenya, tied ridging without organic inputs was insufficient in soil moisture conservation since there was little or no rainwater to be held in the basins [ev_soil_water_retention_ndun23_1]: structures store rain, they cannot make it. A review found no significant effect of infiltration trenches on soil moisture because only four studies provided sufficient statistical data [ev_soil_water_retention_locat20_1]. The zaï and half-moon results come with compost in the pits, so the moisture gain cannot be credited to the pit alone [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8], the Indian watershed comparison is a project-commissioned study of a package of soil and water conservation structures [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2], and the Brazilian tied-furrow trial ran a single season at a station of the agency that promotes the technology [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9]. Soil moisture is read as a component of water stress, not water stress itself. Those best-practice arms are bundled: planting pits, basins or ripper-with-ridging (the capture element, which is the practice here) come with reduced tillage and mostly with fertiliser, and tillage alone is not water harvesting [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_1]. The trial-level readings are weaker: the authors find no clear tillage effect on rain water productivity in Kenya, no clear effects of tillage in Ethiopia (where the gains that do show come with fertilised treatments), and only a tendency of improvement in semi-arid Tanzania [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_5, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_4]. effect_mechanism: Terraces and check dams hold water where it is needed. A global terracing synthesis finds terraced sites more efficient than slopes at reducing runoff and conserving soil water (e.g., soil moisture recharge), with a mean δsm of 1.2 [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1]. A terracing review cites Posthumus and Stroosnijder (2010) finding that the soil stays humid for longer on terraces than on sloping fields, and that ponding on very flat terrace beds increases infiltration [ev_soil_moisture_arna15_7], and a check-dam review reports that check dams that store seasonal runoff solve local scarcity in supply [ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1].
conditionality: Both sources pool cases from high- and lower-income countries, so the cell does not isolate the low-income target [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1, ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1]. The terracing ratio is an unweighted mean across extracted cases, and soil moisture is read as a component of water stress rather than water stress itself [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1]. The check-dam and terrace-moisture findings are secondary citations within reviews, and the same terrace study reports infiltration capacity itself not particularly affected by terracing [ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1, ev_soil_moisture_arna15_7]. conditionality: The benefit is real but its size is not stated, hence the slight class. The cistern evidence is an interview account and a census-based inference with no counterfactual, and the subsurface-dam supply is intermittent [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5, ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1]. effect_mechanism: Watershed treatment reduces reliance on outside supply: participating villages in India saw reduced water transportation by tanker compared with nonparticipating villages [ev_water_access_deficit_verm19_1], and an agency review credits consumption and production cisterns in semi-arid Brazil with a significant contribution to wider access to water [ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1]. In India, discharge of springs and streams rose in treated watersheds: a sample study in Himachal Pradesh reports a 40 percent increase in water discharge in spring and stream sources [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1], and the Uttarakhand project achieved an average 21 percent increase in water discharge from perennial water sources in sampled micro-watersheds, against a target of 25 percent [ev_water_regulation_utk22_6]. Measured soil moisture adds a field route: a meta-analysis of in-situ practices finds they improve soil moisture retention by 59%, with soil/stone bunds at an SMD of 76.4% [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_1, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_3]; in Burkina Faso zaï of 30–40 cm diameter and 1-m half-moons retained moisture for 2-3 weeks through dry spells [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]; and Indian project watersheds showed an increase in soil moisture content by 30.5 percent compared to the IWMP sites [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2]. The water-productivity evidence points the same way: FAO compilers list improved water use efficiency among the main benefits of rainwater harvesting, the WOCAT guideline authors find that all water harvesting groups indicate improved water use efficiency, mostly high to medium, through reduced evaporation loss and better soil water availability, and a review sentence, citing earlier work, says capture approaches often lead also to higher water productivity because denser canopies shade the soil [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1].

effect_mechanism: Micro-catchments concentrate runoff from the bare ground between basins into the planted area, so more water stays in the root zone. In the eastern drylands of Ethiopia, a study by Abdulkadir and Schultz cited by Biazin et al. found mean soil moisture 31% higher in the wet season and 24% higher in the dry season in tree-and-grass plots fed by micro-catchments [ev_soil_moisture_biaz12_1]. conditionality: The Ethiopian figure is a secondary citation, and the Vallerani units are practitioner ratings with the well-level rise a community report. The evidence measures soil water in the field, not household water supply. No measured in-field soil-water contrast for micro-catchments is in the pool apart from the secondary Ethiopian citation; that is what is missing.

In the eastern drylands of Ethiopia, a study by Abdulkadir and Schultz cited by Biazin et al. found mean soil moisture 31% higher in the wet season and 24% higher in the dry season in tree-and-grass plots fed by micro-catchments [ev_soil_moisture_biaz12_1]. effect_mechanism: Sand dams, check dams, subsurface dams, ponds and production cisterns store water in sand, soil or tanks and recharge local groundwater, extending the months of water access and keeping livestock watered when other sources dry up. WOCAT compilers judge sand dams in Kenya, an on-farm pond in Cambodia and a haffir, gabions and check dams in Somalia to improve water collection, quantity or availability: sand dams capture excess flood flows, the pond collects rainwater and groundwater, and the Somali structures slow runoff and improve infiltration [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1537_2012_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_2844_2017_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_2844_2017_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7778_2026_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7778_2026_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7778_2026_water_availability]. In Zimbabwe the months per year water could be collected at sand-dam sites rose from 6.5 to 10.9 after construction, and from 5.8 to 9.7 in a drought year, while in Kenya the average distance to a water source fell from 3 to 1 km [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lasage08_1]. A check-dam review reports that check dams storing seasonal runoff solve local supply scarcity; traditional rainwater ponds in South Korea reduced the occurrence of water deficit from 30 to 20% [ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1]. Water productivity, the grain produced per unit of rain, is a route by which capture eases water stress. Supplemental irrigation from a Kenyan runoff dam with fertiliser raised rain and irrigation water-use efficiency from 2.1 to 4.1 kg of grain per mm per hectare against the farmers' control [ev_rain_water_productivity_barr05_9], and supplementary irrigation in semi-arid Zimbabwe raised water productivity from 1.75 to 2.3 kg per cubic metre (Kahinda et al. 2007) [ev_rain_water_productivity_dile13_6, ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5]. In Burkina Faso, water-harvesting reservoirs are used for livestock and household needs during periods of domestic water scarcity [ev_water_access_deficit_foxr03_7].
conditionality: Many Kenyan sand dams lack capacity to supply even one household through the dry season, and only part of assessed dams would hold enough water for reported beneficiaries [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3, ev_water_access_deficit_neuf17_1]. Several literature units are review citations, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements. The Zimbabwean sand-dam figures rely on recall of conditions before construction [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2]. The check-dam and pond findings are secondary citations in reviews, and the Korean result is modelled in a high-income setting [ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1]. The Somali haffir compiler itself records improved local water availability with little benefit downstream [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7777_2026_water_availability]. Groundwater-recharge evidence for these structures now sits in the catchment water yield rows, which also answer what upstream capture does to water downstream. In Burkina Faso, overall water-use efficiency of rain plus irrigation did not rise with supplemental irrigation, so the extra yield came with extra water [ev_rain_water_productivity_foxr03_6]; the Kenyan efficiency gain also carries fertiliser, and the Zimbabwe figure is a survey-and-modelling estimate cited second-hand [ev_rain_water_productivity_barr05_9, ev_rain_water_productivity_dile13_6].

justification.pool_note: This row draws on 22 evidence unit(s) from 16 source(s); the weighting counts sources, not units, so several findings from one paper do not multiply its say.
justification.mechanism: Sand dams, check dams, subsurface dams, ponds and production cisterns store water in sand, soil or tanks and recharge local groundwater, extending the months of water access and keeping livestock watered when other sources dry up. WOCAT compilers judge sand dams in Kenya, an on-farm pond in Cambodia and a haffir, gabions and check dams in Somalia to improve water collection, quantity or availability: sand dams capture excess flood flows, the pond collects rainwater and groundwater, and the Somali structures slow runoff and improve infiltration [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1537_2012_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_2844_2017_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_2844_2017_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7778_2026_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7778_2026_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7778_2026_water_availability]. In Zimbabwe the months per year water could be collected at sand-dam sites rose from 6.5 to 10.9 after construction, and from 5.8 to 9.7 in a drought year, while in Kenya the average distance to a water source fell from 3 to 1 km [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lasage08_1]. A check-dam review reports that check dams storing seasonal runoff solve local supply scarcity; traditional rainwater ponds in South Korea reduced the occurrence of water deficit from 30 to 20% [ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1]. Water productivity, the grain produced per unit of rain, is a route by which capture eases water stress. Supplemental irrigation from a Kenyan runoff dam with fertiliser raised rain and irrigation water-use efficiency from 2.1 to 4.1 kg of grain per mm per hectare against the farmers' control [ev_rain_water_productivity_barr05_9], and supplementary irrigation in semi-arid Zimbabwe raised water productivity from 1.75 to 2.3 kg per cubic metre (Kahinda et al. 2007) [ev_rain_water_productivity_dile13_6, ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5]. In Burkina Faso, water-harvesting reservoirs are used for livestock and household needs during periods of domestic water scarcity [ev_water_access_deficit_foxr03_7].
justification.conditionality: Many Kenyan sand dams lack capacity to supply even one household through the dry season, and only part of assessed dams would hold enough water for reported beneficiaries [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3, ev_water_access_deficit_neuf17_1]. Several literature units are review citations, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements. The Zimbabwean sand-dam figures rely on recall of conditions before construction [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2]. The check-dam and pond findings are secondary citations in reviews, and the Korean result is modelled in a high-income setting [ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1]. The Somali haffir compiler itself records improved local water availability with little benefit downstream [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7777_2026_water_availability]. Groundwater-recharge evidence for these structures now sits in the catchment water yield rows, which also answer what upstream capture does to water downstream. In Burkina Faso, overall water-use efficiency of rain plus irrigation did not rise with supplemental irrigation, so the extra yield came with extra water [ev_rain_water_productivity_foxr03_6]; the Kenyan efficiency gain also carries fertiliser, and the Zimbabwe figure is a survey-and-modelling estimate cited second-hand [ev_rain_water_productivity_barr05_9, ev_rain_water_productivity_dile13_6].

effect_mechanism: Terraces and stone lines capture and retain rainwater on slopes, and stone lines contribute to increased infiltration of rainwater into the soil, thereby replenishing water resources [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6610_2022_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6610_2022_water_availability]. Measured soil moisture supports this: a meta-analysis gives terraces an SMD of 40.5% for soil moisture retention [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_6], a global terracing synthesis finds terraced sites more efficient than slopes at conserving soil water, with a mean δsm of 1.2 [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1], and conversion of slopeland to leveled fields in China increased moisture retention [ev_soil_water_retention_iegchn07_2]. Water productivity, the grain produced per unit of rain, is a route by which capture eases water stress. The FAO compilers rate improving water productivity for the cross-slope barrier group at the middle mark of their scale [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3]. In Ethiopia's Anjene catchment, terraces improved the water productivity of teff, barley and maize by at least 100% against un-terraced plots [ev_rain_water_productivity_adgo13_7]. A review of farming terraces notes that the soil stays humid for longer on terraces than on sloping fields, and that a very flat terrace bed lets rain pond, reducing runoff and increasing infiltration [ev_soil_moisture_arna15_7].
conditionality: The Tunisian stone-line units are practitioner judgements, and catchment modelling in Peru found no difference in crop water distribution with partial terracing [ev_water_regulation_willem21_1]. Abandoned or degraded terraces worsen water regulation [ev_water_regulation_willem21_2]. The recharge estimates for terraces and contour ridges now sit in the terracing catchment water yield row. The terracing ratio is an unweighted mean across extracted cases from mixed-income countries [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1], and the Chinese finding comes from an independent World Bank evaluation reporting project monitoring with no control [ev_soil_water_retention_iegchn07_2]. That is a compiler judgement for a group spanning earth bunds, stone lines, vegetative strips and fanya juu terraces, direction only [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3]. The same review cites work finding that the infiltration capacity of the soil is not particularly affected by terracing (Posthumus and Stroosnijder, 2010), so the gain comes from water held longer on the flat bed rather than a change in the soil [ev_soil_moisture_arna15_7]. The Anjene figure compares long-maintained terraces with un-terraced plots at a single catchment where farmers also use fertiliser [ev_rain_water_productivity_adgo13_7].
